# SeedForge

> A client-side Minecraft seed finder for Java and Bedrock Edition. Pick the
> structures and biomes you want, give each one its own maximum distance from
> world spawn, optionally require two of them to generate near each other, and
> search for seeds that satisfy all of it at once.

Live tool: https://fwsoapy.github.io/seedforge/
Source: https://github.com/fwsoapy/seedforge
Licence: MIT

## What it does

- Searches Minecraft world seeds for a combination of structures and biomes
  near spawn. A seed only matches when every criterion is satisfied.
- Each criterion carries its own distance limit, so you can ask for a village
  within 100 blocks and a ruined portal within 500 in the same search.
- Proximity rules add conditions between two picks, for example a bastion
  within 300 blocks of where a ruined portal drops you in the Nether.
- Filters go down to ruined portal type, placement and template, bastion
  remnant type, stronghold ring, and village biome type.
- Java Edition 1.7 through 26.2, and Bedrock Edition 1.18 and later.

## How it works

World generation is deterministic, so structure positions are computed rather
than looked up. There is no seed database and no backend. Java generation comes
from Cubiomes (https://github.com/Cubitect/cubiomes) compiled to WebAssembly;
Bedrock structure placement is implemented in the repository directly, because
Cubiomes does not cover it. Searching runs in Web Workers, one per CPU core,
entirely in the visitor's browser.

## Accuracy

Results are computed estimates with documented limits, listed under "Accuracy
and limitations" in the tool and in the repository README. Notable ones: some
1.18+ structures depend on surface height that Cubiomes approximates; biome
criteria are grid-sampled so a very small patch can be missed; ravines and
individual caves cannot be searched at all.

Mojang Studios or Microsoft.
